CHECK · CHOOSE ONE

Which statement best describes photosynthesis?

Green plants use light energy to make glucose and release oxygen.
Green plants use glucose to make light energy.
Green plants absorb food from the soil and release carbon dioxide.
Green plants use oxygen to break down glucose only in darkness.
Go to the Check button

Move the light slider and watch both bars. Set the glucose production to 4 units.

Aim for: Glucose production = 4

Glucose production
4 units
Oxygen production
3 units
LIGHT INTENSITY
50 %
Solved

WHAT YOU JUST FOUND

Green plants use light energy to make glucose, releasing oxygen as they do so. This process is called photosynthesis; the glucose provides food for the plant and, through food chains, for other organisms.

Photosynthesis: making food using light

Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose, releasing oxygen as well. This matters because plants use the glucose for growth and energy, while other organisms depend on plants for food and on the oxygen released for respiration.
Go deeper

Move the light slider and watch both bars. Set the glucose production to 6 units.

Aim for: Glucose production = 6

Glucose production
6 units
Oxygen production
3 units
LIGHT INTENSITY
60 %
Solved

WHAT YOU JUST FOUND

At 60% light intensity, the plant produces 6 units of glucose and 3 units of oxygen. More light allows more photosynthesis, so both outputs rise together.
